item.text: I’ve got enough to synthesize. The record looks mixed on reassurance and institution-building, but the dominant 2024 pattern is protest policing and legal measures that amplified fear rather than only reducing it.

# Bola Ahmed Tinubu, 2024: 3B.6 research note

Bottom line: Tinubu did take some steps that lowered immediate insecurity through dialogue, policing reform, and institution-based security coordination. But the year’s dominant pattern, especially around the August protests, was a broad fear climate: forceful rhetoric, heavy policing, treason charges, and cybercrime / subversion laws used in ways rights groups and Reuters described as intimidating or punitive.

## Accepted claims

- [President Tinubu urges state policing as remedy to insecurity](https://statehouse.gov.ng/my-resolve-to-enhance-nigerias-security-unwavering-president-tinubu/) — State House, April 22, 2024. Tinubu framed state policing as a way to improve accountability and better fit local security needs. This is positive evidence for reducing insecurity through institutional design rather than raw coercion. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.4`, `3B.5`.

- [Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462) — Reuters via Investing.com, July 31, 2024. The government said it was open to dialogue even as security forces deployed in major cities. This is mixed evidence: it shows some effort to manage unrest without immediate total shutdown, but the simultaneous deployment also signaled coercive readiness. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.2`.

- [President Tinubu’s Broadcast on the Nationwide Protest](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-broadcast-on-the-nationwide-protest/) — State House, August 4, 2024. Tinubu acknowledged deaths, destruction, and legitimate hopes among protesters, asked for protests to be suspended to allow dialogue, and told law enforcement to protect lives and property responsibly. This is the strongest positive evidence that he tried to reduce fear without relying only on repression, though it was partial and did not concede protesters’ demands. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.5`.

- [Tinubu calls for suspension of sanctions on Guinea, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-calls-for-suspension-of-sanctions-on-guinea-mali-niger-burkina-faso/) — State House, February 24, 2024. Tinubu argued ECOWAS should stop treating itself as an enemy and should pursue “a better path” through negotiation and improved governance. That is direct evidence of de-escalatory regional management that can reduce insecurity rather than intensify it. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `2B.10`, `2B.1`.

- [Nigeria: Police used excessive force to violently quash #Endbadgovernance protests](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/) — Amnesty International, November 28, 2024. Amnesty reported at least 24 protesters killed, over 1,200 detained, and torture and arbitrary arrests during the August protests, and it said authorities denied wrongdoing. This is strong negative evidence that state action increased fear and insecurity rather than only reducing it. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.4`, `3B.5`.

- [Nigeria: Protesters Charged with Treason](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/09/06/nigeria-protesters-charged-treason) — Human Rights Watch, September 6, 2024. HRW said protesters were charged with treason, held for long periods, and subjected to due-process concerns, including minors. This is strong evidence of a broader political fear climate created through punitive legal measures. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.1`, `3B.2`, `3B.5`.

- [Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting](https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/) — Committee to Protect Journalists, October 3, 2024. CPJ reported that four journalists were charged under the Cybercrimes Act despite the February reform, showing continued use of security-law tools against press activity. This supports the negative side because fear and legal risk were extended into media oversight. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.2`, `3B.3`.

- [Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024 Country Report](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024) — Freedom House, 2024. Freedom House said the Cybercrimes Act’s cyberstalking provision had been frequently used to arrest or imprison journalists and activists, even after amendment. This is negative evidence that legal controls were still functioning as intimidation rather than narrow public safety tools. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.2`, `3B.3`.

- [Nigerian lawmakers withdraw proposed subversive law after public outcry](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/nigeria-considers-tough-penalties-for-subversive-acts-under-proposed-law-3571782) — Reuters via Investing.com, August 14, 2024. Reuters reported lawmakers withdrew a proposed Counter Subversion Bill after backlash that it was aimed at cracking down on dissent after the protests. The existence of the bill itself is negative evidence for a fear climate, even though withdrawal is a partial corrective. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.3`.

- [Tinubu: We will not allow anyone to undermine our security, killers of soldiers in Delta State will face certain justice](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-we-will-no-allow-anyone-to-undermine-our-security-killers-of-soldiers-in-delta-state-will-face-certain-justice/) — State House, March 21, 2024. Tinubu promised “certain justice” for attackers and said the government would not tolerate attacks on military infrastructure. This is understandable as a response to real violence, but the rhetoric is still coercive and contributes to a hard-security climate. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.1`.

- [President Tinubu’s statement on the killings of soldiers in Aba](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-statement-on-the-killings-of-soldiers-in-aba/) — State House, June 2, 2024. Tinubu said the government would “come down heavily” and “crush” violent non-state actors. This is negative evidence for the lens because it signals punitive force as a primary answer to insecurity. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.1`.

- [Nigeria security forces deploy, government offers dialogue as protests loom](https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/nigeria-security-forces-deploy-government-offers-dialogue-as-protests-loom-3546462) — Reuters via Investing.com, July 31, 2024. Reuters said authorities feared the protests could turn violent, and the preemptive deployment of security forces reinforced a climate of apprehension. This is mixed evidence, but it leans negative on whether the response lowered fear without replacing it with coercive pressure. Question IDs: `3B.6`; other: `3B.5`, `3B.2`.

## Search gap

- I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Tinubu declared a broad state of emergency or ran a formal nationwide emergency regime.
- I also did not find strong evidence of a sustained, rights-protective public strategy that clearly reduced fear while avoiding coercive overreach.
- The available record is mostly about protest policing, treason/cybercrime enforcement, and reactive dialogue. That makes the lens look mixed at best and more negative than positive overall.
